recipes.name: Chicken Cordon Bleu Casserole
ingredients_raw: 2 pounds skinless, boneless chicken breast halves - cut into chunks
1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of chicken soup

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Beat egg and 1/2 cup milk together until combined. Stir in the chicken chunks to coat, then drain, and coat with bread crumbs. Heat oil in a large skillet to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Fry breaded chicken cubes in hot oil until golden brown on all sides, then remove, and drain on paper towels.
Place chicken cubes in a glass baking dish, along with the Swiss cheese, and ham. Stir together the soup with 1 cup milk, pour over casserole.
Bake in preheated oven until golden brown and bubbly, about 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken Cordon Bleu Casserole
raw_recipe.description: I love making casseroles, and this one's so simple. The chicken breasts, Swiss cheese, and ham are cubed, rather than stuffed and rolled, giving you all the flavor of Cordon Bleu in much less time.

review.reviewBody: I doubled this recipe and froze the ham, chicken and swiss. The first batch was really runny, but tasted great. For the second batch, I put some uncooked rice underneath the chicken, ham, cheese and soup mixture. The rice soaked up all of the juices and was super yummy. I think it would work well with stuffing mix as well.

After I tweaked this recipe - it was fantastic. I cut the recipe down to 4 servings as there is only me. I also fried the chicken in a non-stick skillet with 1 tablespoon of butter - not oil. For the sauce, I only used 1 can of Healthy Request soup and 1/4 can of milk so it was not runny at all. But I did add 1 tablespoon minced garlic, 1 tablespoon Mrs. Dash Seasoning and 1/2 onion grated to the sauce - cause I wanted this to taste good. Served with a green salad. Yum. Will make this again.

This is a pretty decent base recipe. I took suggestions of many -- added cooked rice in pan bottom; thyme, garlic powder, parmesean cheese in chicken coating; added 2 tbsp mayo to egg wash to thicken; plus I used turkey ham instead of regular ham. It still could use a little extra flavor but havent decided what the addition will be. Thanks!

Great basic idea, but I am lazy and took some shortcuts. I cut the chicken into 1 1/2 inch cubes, tossed them in a little olive oil, shook them in a plastic bag of bread crumbs and baked them until they were done. 
Lined the bottom of the dish with 1/2 inch uncooked rice then the ham, chicken, and cheese. Used 2 cans of soup and 1 cup of milk. Topped it with some crushed Ritz Crackers. There were no leftovers.

I don't get the canned soup part, nor the point of breading the chicken prior. It adds so much more sodium to the dish where the ham is salty enough. I flash fry the chicken and ham , pour it in casserole dish, toss it a bit with a few tablespoons of flour -- along with warmed milk it will thicken on its own when baked. I add mushrooms (pre-rendered so not to add more liquid)and top with buttered bread crumbs -- it is gorgeous, creamy, cheesy and flavorful.

after reading all the reviews i decided to not switch things but make it more for my family. we are trying to eat healthier now so we did not coat and fry the chicken. we just cooked the chicken in the pan and then cubed it up. because ham is a natura water "holder" i quickly cooked the ham in a pan first to drain most of the water out of it. i used low sodium cream of chicken soup. i put 1/2 cup of milk with the soup instead of 1 cup. i put 1/2 cup cheese in the mix and 1/2 cup on top. then coverd with a small amount of breadcrumbs. the casserole was not runny at all and tasted very good! the only complaint i have it that this recipe says for 8 people. i have a family of 4. my husband and daughter eat quite a bit and this casserole only covered the 4 of us. depending on what you call a serving size, i would double up on the ingredients if you have more than 4 people in your family. thanks to everyone who put in suggestions!!

This recipe is kick-butt! The first time I made it, it came out a little runny so I took the advice of some other reviewers and cut the milk to 1/2 c. and used 2 cans of soup instead of one. One other thing I did differently was layer the bottom of my pie dish with green peas-- it came out perfect! My husband does a little dance everytime I ask him if he wants this on the menu for the week :) Thank you for sharing!

This is 5 stars with reviewers changes. I halved this recipe and cooked it in a casserole dish. I used 1 egg & 1/4 cup whole milk for egg wash. I used 3/4 cup of italian bread crumbs. 4 oz of swiss cheese. I used half milk and half sour cream. It was not runny at all. It actually looked very appetizing unlike the picture above.

I did it differently. I didn't fry anything instead I mixed the ham, chicken and 2 cans of cream of chicken and filled one can with milk so it was thicker.
Then I poured that in a pan layered it with swiss cheese and topped with bread crumbs. I don't like frying because of the added calories. We all loved it.

I just made this last night when I screwed up pounding out my chicken for traditional cordon bleu. Instead of a cream soup (which I didn't have!), I made white sauce with a hint of Dijon and added the Swiss cheese to the sauce. I did not bread the chicken first, but sauteed in an olive oil and butter blend and drained on paper towels. I followed the rest of the recipe pretty much, except I sprinkled a good dose of buttered bread crumbs on the top of the casserole.. not too bad!! Overall, the idea of this recipe saved dinner. I served this with sauteed broccoli spears and roasted garlic mashed potatoes.

Very good, filling casserole. I chose to brown the chicken instead of frying it and used the bread crumbs for a crust on top. I upped the amount of ham to 12 ounces, and I also used the half cup of sour cream, half cup of milk alteration many on here have recommended. Perfect consistency. I think I'll add some mushrooms next time to see if that makes it even better.

I made this recipe as written using gluten free ingredients (cream of chicken and bread crumbs). It was easy to put together and I did have some concerns with the cream of chicken soup based on reviews, but I had no issues with the recipe having too much liquid (maybe because I used gluten free items). The end result, my husband loved, but my daughter and I were on the meh side. The recipe could benefit from the simple seasoning that classic chicken cordon blue has or at the very least seasoned bread crumbs.

Made the changes as noted by others; used Greek yogurt instead of sour cream and provolone instead of Swiss, because that's what I had. Easy recipe compared to others I've seen where you make your own white sauce.
Like others, I used 1/2 cup sour cream and 1/2 cup milk instead of 1 cup milk. Delicious!
We love chicken cordon bleu. This recipe is the best one we have tried we won't make it any other way now.

This turned out great, although I modified the meat quantities to use less chicken and an equal amount of ham. I also sprinkled bread crumbs on top. I served it with a side of green beans and my family cleaned their plates! Very yummy. Prep time takes longer than stated.
This was delicious and easy to make!! Will definitely be making this again!!

Wonderful flavors! After reading reviews, I used soup and sour cream. It still was runny when I cut into it. Next time I make this I'll increase the Swiss cheese and pre-cook the cubed ham . Thank you for a wonderful alternative to trying to roll chicken around the filling.
